issues.description: No input validation for the 'query' parameter. If query is null, undefined, or not a string, the function will fail or produce unexpected results.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation at the start of the function: 'if (!query || typeof query !== 'string') { return []; }' or throw an error for invalid input.

issues.description: No null/undefined check before accessing 'todo.text'. If a todo object lacks a 'text' property or if text is null/undefined, this will throw a TypeError.
issues.suggestion: Add defensive checks: 'if (todo && todo.text && todo.text.indexOf(query) !== -1) { ... }' or use optional chaining: 'if (todo?.text?.indexOf(query) !== -1) { ... }'.

issues.description: Using 'var' instead of 'const' or 'let' for variable declaration. The variable 'results' is never reassigned and should be declared with 'const'.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'var results = []' with 'const results = []'. Modern JavaScript (ES6+) uses 'const' for variables that are not reassigned and 'let' for those that are.

issues.description: Using traditional for loop instead of modern array iteration methods. This is less readable and more error-prone.
issues.suggestion: Replace the for loop with 'all.filter(todo => todo.text.indexOf(query) !== -1)' or use 'for...of' loop for better readability: 'for (const todo of all) { ... }'.

issues.description: Using 'indexOf' for string searching. Modern JavaScript provides 'includes()' method which is more semantic and readable.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'todo.text.indexOf(query) !== -1' with 'todo.text.includes(query)' for better readability and clarity of intent.

issues.description: Case-sensitive search may not match user expectations. Searching for 'TODO' won't match 'todo' in the text.
issues.suggestion: Consider implementing case-insensitive search: 'todo.text.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())' unless case-sensitivity is a requirement.

issues.description: No input validation for the 'query' parameter in searchTodosByStatus function.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: 'if (!query || typeof query !== 'string') { return []; }'.

issues.description: No validation for the 'done' parameter. If 'done' is not a boolean, the strict equality check (===) might not work as expected.
issues.suggestion: Add type validation: 'if (typeof done !== 'boolean') { throw new TypeError('done parameter must be a boolean'); }' or provide a default value.

issues.description: Code duplication between searchTodos and searchTodosByStatus. The second function duplicates the search logic with an additional filter condition.
issues.suggestion: Refactor to reduce duplication: Make searchTodosByStatus call searchTodos and filter the results, or create a common helper function that both can use.

issues.description: The searchTodos function performs a linear scan through all todos on every call, which could be inefficient for large datasets.
issues.suggestion: Consider caching results or implementing indexing for frequently searched queries. For very large datasets, consider using a search library or database full-text search.

codeQuality.summary: The file src/search.js contains multiple significant issues across security, performance, maintainability, and style categories. Critical concerns include: (1) High bug-risk due to lack of input validation and null checks that could cause runtime errors; (2) Outdated ES5 syntax using 'var' instead of modern 'const'/'let' declarations throughout; (3) Code duplication between the two search functions; (4) Missing defensive programming practices like null/undefined checks before property access. The code would benefit from modernization to ES6+ standards, implementing proper input validation, adding null safety checks, reducing code duplication through refactoring, and adding comprehensive documentation.

refactorings.summary: The search.js fiximately 15 lines while improving readability, maintainability, and making the code more idiomatic to modern JavaScript.

issues.description: The search query parameter 'req.query.q' is passed directly to searchTodos() without any validation, sanitization, or type checking. If searchTodos uses this parameter in database queries, it could enable injection attacks.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation before passing to searchTodos. Example: const query = typeof req.query.q === 'string' ? req.query.q.trim() : ''; if (query.length > 200) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Query too long' }); res.json(searchTodos(query));

issues.description: Missing query parameter validation: The endpoint doesn't check if 'req.query.q' exists or is defined. Passing undefined/null to searchTodos() could cause unexpected behavior or crashes.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit validation: if (!req.query.q) { return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Search query parameter "q" is required' }); }

issues.description: No rate limiting on search endpoint: Search operations can be expensive, and this endpoint lacks rate limiting. Attackers could perform denial-of-service attacks by sending numerous search requests.
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting middleware specifically for the search endpoint, or apply application-wide rate limiting. Consider using express-rate-limit: const searchLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, max: 100 }); app.get('/todos/search', searchLimiter, ...);

issues.description: Missing input length restriction: Long query strings could cause performance degradation or buffer overflow issues. There's no maximum length validation on the search query.
issues.suggestion: Add length validation: const query = req.query.q || ''; if (query.length > 200) { return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Search query exceeds maximum length of 200 characters' }); }

issues.description: No error handling: If searchTodos() throws an error (e.g., database connection failure, malformed query), the application will crash or return a 500 error without proper error information.
issues.suggestion: Wrap in try-catch: try { const results = searchTodos(req.query.q); res.json(results); } catch (error) { console.error('Search error:', error); res.status(500).json({ error: 'Search failed' }); }

issues.description: Missing XSS protection for search results: If searchTodos returns user-generated content that includes the search query, it could be vulnerable to reflected XSS attacks when rendered in the client.
issues.suggestion: Ensure searchTodos properly escapes or sanitizes user input before including it in responses. Consider using Content-Security-Policy headers and ensure the frontend properly escapes output.

issues.description: Route ordering issue: The '/todos/search' route is defined after '/todos' GET route. While this specific case works because '/todos/search' is more specific, adding future routes like '/todos/:id' before '/todos/search' would break search functionality.
issues.suggestion: Move the search route before any parameterized routes, or consider restructuring to use query parameters on the main route: app.get('/todos', (req, res) => { if (req.query.q) return res.json(searchTodos(req.query.q)); res.json(listTodos()); });

codeQuality.summary: The new search endpoint (lines 4 and 14-16) introduces several critical security vulnerabilities. Most concerning is the lack of input validation on req.query.q, which could enable injection attacks (CRITICAL). The endpoint also lacks required parameter validation (HIGH), rate limiting (HIGH), and proper error handling (MEDIUM). The code is vulnerable to DoS attacks through expensive search operations and could expose XSS vulnerabilities if search results include unsanitized user input. Immediate action required: Add input validation, sanitization, length restrictions, error handling, and rate limiting before deploying to production.

refactorings.summary: The search endpoint implementation is minimal and lacks essential production-ready features. The highest-impact improvements are: (1) adding input validation to prevent undefined/invalid queries, (2) implementing try-catch error handling to prevent server crashes, and (3) extracting handler logic into a testable function. All suggestions are behavior-preserving when valid input is provided, while adding robustness for edge cases and error conditions.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive input validation for the search endpoint. The req.query.q parameter is passed directly to searchTodos() without any validation, sanitization, or type checking. This could enable injection attacks, cause runtime crashes with undefined/null values, and create DoS vulnerabilities with excessively long queries.

Implement proper error handling throughout the search functionality. Both the search endpoint and search functions lack null/undefined checks before property access (todo.text), which will cause TypeError crashes. The endpoint also needs try-catch blocks to handle searchTodos() failures gracefully.

Add comprehensive test coverage for the new search functionality. Currently, there are ZERO tests for both src/search.js and the new search endpoint in src/server.js. Critical test cases needed: valid search queries, missing/invalid query parameters, null/undefined handling, empty results, special characters, and error scenarios.

Implement rate limiting on the search endpoint to prevent DoS attacks. Search operations can be expensive, and without rate limiting, attackers could overwhelm the server with numerous search requests. Also add maximum query length validation (recommend 200 characters) to prevent performance degradation.

Modernize the search.js code from ES5 to ES6+ standards. Replace all 'var' declarations with 'const'/'let', replace traditional for loops with array methods (filter), and replace indexOf() with includes(). This will improve readability, reduce error-proneness, and align with modern JavaScript best practices.

Eliminate code duplication between searchTodos and searchTodosByStatus functions. Extract common text matching logic into a reusable helper function, or have searchTodosByStatus compose with searchTodos. This creates a single source of truth and makes the code easier to maintain and test.

Consider implementing case-insensitive search. The current implementation uses indexOf/includes which is case-sensitive, so searching for 'TODO' won't match 'todo'. Case-insensitive search typically provides better user experience unless case-sensitivity is a specific requirement.

For production use with large datasets, consider implementing search optimizations such as result caching, query debouncing, or indexing. The current linear scan approach (O(n)) may become a bottleneck as the todo list grows.
